title: Multi-Timeframe Thinking
hook: Higher timeframes give context. Lower timeframes reveal detail.
mission: By the end of this lesson, you should be able to explain why zooming in changes what you can see, not what's actually happening.

blocks.heading: Every timeframe has a job. You just don't know what it is yet.

beats.heading: Context, then detail
beats.body: Higher timeframes give you context — the bigger picture of what price is doing. Lower timeframes reveal detail — the smaller moves inside that picture.

beats.heading: One lesson at a time
beats.body: Later in the Academy, you'll learn exactly how AGHF assigns a specific job to each timeframe. For now, just get comfortable with the idea that they're telling different parts of the same story.

blocks.heading: Build the zoom order
blocks.prompt: Tap the timeframes in the order you'd generally check them — biggest picture first.
blocks.successFeedback: That's the general zoom order — biggest picture first, most detail last. You'll learn the exact job each one does later in the Academy.
blocks.failFeedback: Not quite the order — think biggest picture first, most zoomed-in last.

blocks.heading: What's the risk in her thinking?
blocks.scenario: A trader treats every timeframe as if it should give her the same kind of answer.

options.label: She'll get confused when a detailed view and a big-picture view naturally look different
options.feedback: Exactly — expecting every timeframe to answer the same question leads to unnecessary confusion.

options.label: There's no risk — all timeframes should always agree perfectly
options.feedback: Timeframes don't have to agree perfectly at every moment.

blocks.quote: I'm not going to hand you the whole framework in one lesson. Right now, just notice that a higher timeframe and a lower timeframe are telling you different parts of the same story.

questions.question: A trader forms her entire directional bias off the 1-minute chart alone, ignoring the 4H. What's the risk in doing that?
options: She's using a detailed, zoomed-in view to make a bigger-picture decision it wasn't built to answer
There's no risk — every timeframe shows the same picture
The 1-minute chart is always more reliable than higher timeframes
questions.why: The 1M is built for detail, not for establishing the overall directional story.

questions.question: The clean beginner flow is bigger picture, then structure, then ___ detail last.
questions.why: Entry detail comes last, after the bigger picture and structure are established.

blocks.prompt: Imagine another AGHF girl asks: "Why not just trade off the 1-minute chart the whole time?" How would you explain it to her?

takeaways: Higher timeframes give context; lower timeframes reveal detail.
Zooming in changes what you can see — not what's actually happening.
A messy lower timeframe doesn't erase a clear higher-timeframe read.
remember: Different timeframes, different parts of the same story.
